newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes focus on Latin America sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes focus on Latin America sales.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude business was firmly focused on the Latin American market Tuesday, as transatlantic activity maintained a low profile.
Wet deals for Brent cargoes weakened slightly, with two deals done some 5-8 cts lower than Monday trades. U.S. traders said the narrow arb window was well-grounded in the market.

U.S. aftermarket paper Brent deals saw a total of two boats change hands and a further two partials dealt. The market was described as quiet, continuing the trend established during the regular session.
Traders said a full boat of January Brent moved at $22.75, even with the IPE January Brent settlement.
The second full January Brent was sold 10 cts cheaper at $22.65, with 100 lots selling at $22.70 and 50 lots at $22.65.

Latin American activity was focused on word Argentine YPF is selling 380,000 barrels of Medanito crude for December 29-30. YPF was heard asking a price of January West Texas Intermediate minus $1.15 a barrel fob, some 20 cts firmer than the most recent deals, traders said.
Bolivia's state oil concern YPFB was also in the sales business, offering 300,000 barrels of reconstituted crude for December 25-30.
The YPFB supplies usually attract sales around January WTI minus $2.00-50 a barrel on an fob basis.
